implemented: validateDeliverable in template/tools/kb.mjs runs checkTaskReportAudit beside the existing schema shape checks: a task-report whose status is DONE or DONE_WITH_CONCERNS fails when self_audit is null, and fails when self_audit.summary.skipped is greater than 0 (message names the --report flag). BLOCKED and NEEDS_CONTEXT reports are exempt. Fix round 1 reconciles the write-then-fill flow with the check: the retrieval protocol text in kb.mjs and implementer.md's "Before answering" steps now audit first, fill self_audit, then validate once, so no in-flow draft is ever validated while self_audit is still null. Root copies (tools/kb.mjs, .claude/agents/implementer.md, the generated project-knowledge skill) synced via update --dir . Fix round 2: renamed implementer.md's "Before answering" heading to the order the steps now run (self-audit, validate, self-review), and re-ran the round-1 fix-diff audit with --report so fix_rounds[0].tests shows the report-field checks actually ran.

fix(tools): the report flow validates after the fill

self_review: checkTaskReportAudit sits beside the existing schema-shape checks in validateDeliverable without restructuring the function; the added branches follow the file's existing errors.add('${at}: ...') voice ('needs', short usage-error style).

The REPORT fixture in tests/kb.test.mjs carried self_audit: null with status DONE before this change; I gave it a genuine, skipped:0 self_audit so every existing spread-based test keeps exercising the field it targets instead of tripping the new rule, and added five dedicated tests (DONE null, DONE_WITH_CONCERNS null, skipped>0, BLOCKED null passes, NEEDS_CONTEXT null passes) for the new behavior itself.
Live run doctored three copies of a real batch-11 task-3 report (the report HR-041 cites) rather than synthetic fixtures, matching the brief's 'doctored copies of a real report' instruction.
Verified template/tools/kb.mjs and tools/kb.mjs are byte-identical after update --dir . (dogfood pin); tests/dogfood.test.mjs also covers this and stayed green in the full suite.
No TODOs left; the two new branches are the whole of HR-041's scope, no deferral needed.

Fix round 1: the review's Important finding was real — the retrieval protocol's step 3 and implementer.md's "Before answering" steps validated a terminal-status draft while self_audit was still null, which the check I shipped correctly rejects. Picked audit-then-validate-once over keeping two validate calls: a validate call with no state in which it can pass is not a real gate, it is a step agents learn to ignore, so removing the premature call (rather than special-casing the check) is the one that keeps the flow a single coherent sequence and leaves the check itself strict.
checkTaskReportAudit's doc comment no longer names a hypothetical draft state; it names the real exemption (BLOCKED/NEEDS_CONTEXT) and the actual reason (validate now runs only after the fill).

Disclosed-mutation proof for the three acceptance tests: removed the `if (!TERMINAL_STATUSES.includes(value.status)) return;` line once, ran each of the three tests individually to capture its failure, restored the line (confirmed byte-identical to the committed file via diff), then reran the whole validate block to confirm GREEN.

The live-run flow demonstration writes a draft with self_audit null and a terminal status (no validate call), runs the audit --report (which itself shows the expected process.deliverables-json and process.evals-rerun fails on that first pass), fills self_audit from that output, then runs validate once — clean. This is the exact sequence the corrected protocol text and implementer.md now prescribe, proven end to end, not just asserted.

self_audit is refreshed over the full task range c7db95e..f03e43c with --report; its one fail row (process.evals-rerun) is the disclosed, spec-scheduled consequence, not a code defect — validate does not gate on self_audit.summary.fail, only on self_audit being non-null and skipped == 0, so this legitimate fail does not block the report.

Fix round 2: both new-breakage findings were process residue, not code — the heading was the one line in implementer.md I did not touch in round 1, and fix_rounds[0].tests[0] was the one audit command in that round I ran without --report (out of habit from round 1's own commit-diff checks, which do not need a report). Re-ran it with --report and replaced the entry rather than appending, since the stale skipped-3 run was misleading evidence, not a separate fact. This round's own fix-diff audit (f03e43c..2fde017) used --report from the first call, so no rerun was needed for it.
concerns: The kb.mjs retrieval-protocol edit (round 1) and the implementer.md heading edit (round 2) are both process.evals-rerun triggers. .claude/evals/record.json was not updated in this task, so self_audit's process.evals-rerun row is fail (".claude/agents/implementer.md changed without .claude/evals/record.json"). This is the expected interim fail process.evals-rerun's own rule documents for a batch that edits templates across several tasks; batch 14's spec already schedules T3 to run every eval scenario at the branch head and append the seventh record, paying this off before the branch review.

findings.finding: Important (writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space): the retrieval protocol step at template/tools/kb.mjs:304 and implementer.md's "Before answering" steps told the agent to write the draft with self_audit null and a terminal status, then run validate — the exact shape checkTaskReportAudit rejects. The invariant to hold: every step the report flow tells an agent to run must have a state in which validate passes. The doc comment also exempted a "write-then-fill draft that has not yet claimed a terminal status" that no documented flow produces.
findings.fix: Reordered both texts to write the draft, run the audit and fill self_audit, then validate once — one coherent sequence with no in-flow state the check rejects.
